blocks.orig: Pemba Island is one of the lesser known islands of the Zanzibar Archipelago. It is however a popular honeymoon destination. If you are looking for rest, tranquility and a romantic atmosphere – this is the place to be! The coral reefs surrounding the entire island form a magnificent playground for snorkelers and divers. The Pemba channel has an impressive marine life and is much like an underwater paradise. Here, you can spot a large variety of colorful fish, sharks, dolphins and even whales. Also, be sure to explore the range of watersport activities. You can choose anything from kayaking, kite surfing and wind surfing to a romantic sunset cruise in a traditional sailing boat.
blocks.html: Among the islands of the Zanzibar Archipelago, Pemba Island is one of the less familiar names. Even so, it is a favourite with honeymooners. Anyone in search of rest, quiet and a romantic setting will feel right at home here! Coral reefs ring the whole island, creating a superb playground for snorkelling and diving. The Pemba channel holds a wealth of marine life and resembles an underwater paradise, where you may come across a great variety of colourful fish, sharks, dolphins and even whales. Make sure you also try the many watersports on offer: kayaking, kite surfing and wind surfing, or a romantic sunset cruise aboard a traditional sailing boat.

blocks.orig:
For a quick glance, have a look at our top three favorite accommodations:
For the Silver category, we offer you Pemba Lodge – Pemba’s first true ecolodge, focused on benefitting its guest, nature and the people of the island. The five simple, yet aesthetic African-style cottages are designed for comfort and a serene oneness with nature.
For our Gold category, we highly recommend The Manta Resort. A remote island hideaway with emphasis on offering you authentic Swahili hospitality with modern comfort. The resort has a submerged room which offers an extraordinary experience you do not want to miss! Moreover, their community efforts to help maintain Pemba’s African heritage, revive its marine life and facilitate unique and sustainable tourism are praiseworthy.
Lastly, the multiple-award-winning boutique hotel Fundu Lagoon is our Platinum category. A small and private mangrove-fringed luxury retreat, only accessible by boat. Here, twelve private hillside and beachfront rooms and suites offer comfort and privacy with its jungle-like surroundings. Honeymooners receive a complimentary bottle of prosecco, a massage and a private dinner to usher in days of pure tranquility, relaxation and romance! Please note: Fundu Lagoon is not suitable for guests below 12 years of age.
blocks.html:
For a quick overview, here are our three favourite places to stay:
In the Silver category we suggest Pemba Lodge – the first genuine ecolodge on Pemba, built to benefit its guests, the natural surroundings and the islanders alike. Its five simple but attractive African-style cottages are made for comfort and a peaceful closeness to nature.
In the Gold category our warm recommendation goes to The Manta Resort. This secluded island retreat pairs genuine Swahili hospitality with modern comfort. Its underwater room is a truly extraordinary experience you should not pass up! On top of that, the resort’s community work – preserving Pemba’s African heritage, restoring marine life and encouraging unique, sustainable tourism – deserves real credit.
Finally, our Platinum category is the boutique hotel Fundu Lagoon, winner of multiple awards. This small, private luxury retreat is fringed by mangroves and can only be reached by boat. Twelve private rooms and suites on the hillside and beachfront combine comfort and seclusion with jungle-like surroundings. Honeymooners are treated to a complimentary bottle of prosecco, a massage and a private dinner as a prelude to days of pure calm, relaxation and romance! Please note: guests under 12 years of age cannot stay at Fundu Lagoon.

blocks.orig: Pemba Island is also called the green island. The main reason is its rich and fertile soil, the lush green hills and the thick vegetation. As such, this untouched island has lots of forests, mango trees and vast clove plantations. A third of the population depends on small scale farming (rice, cloves, cinnamon, bananas, cassava) and fishing. Last but not least, Pemba’s wildlife is not only spectacular below sea level. Bush babies, flying foxes and vervet monkeys roam around the island as well!
blocks.html: Pemba Island also goes by the name of the green island, mainly because of its rich, fertile soil, its lush green hills and its dense vegetation. This unspoilt island is covered in forests, mango trees and extensive clove plantations. Around a third of the inhabitants make a living from small-scale farming (rice, cloves, cinnamon, bananas, cassava) and fishing. And finally: Pemba’s wildlife is not limited to what lies beneath the waves. Bush babies, flying foxes and vervet monkeys also make their home on the island!
